chapters.subtitle: A small pure renderer lowered through data, graphs, contracts, and interchangeable execution.

insights: The swappable thing is the estimator, not the entire renderer.
Retained outputs are part of the product, not debugging exhaust.
tiers.label: Orientation
pitfalls: Reading the L1 graph as a one-box-per-GPU-kernel diagram; logical nodes may fuse.
Treating the UI as the renderer instead of a shell over deterministic cooks.
prose: Think of the project as a laboratory instrument. Scene and pipeline data describe the experiment; pure estimator contracts perform it; a backend executes it; retained records explain what happened.

The four L-layers are lowering boundaries, not four independent applications. The shell surrounds them with cameras, progressive state, files, and UI without leaking I/O or wall-clock behavior into the estimator.
tiers.summary: restir-lab is one renderer whose sampling strategy evolves while its scene, output, replay, and inspection spine stays recognizable.

insights: Compilation is orchestration and lifetime analysis, not a general shader compiler.
Display-only and layout edits must not invalidate semantic render state.
tiers.label: Working model
pitfalls: Adding arbitrary Python operators would break portability and validation.
Committing a delay before all terminals finish would expose partial-frame history.
prose: A selected-terminal graph session compiles only required nodes, tracks resource lifetimes, shares upstream work, and commits frame or accumulation delays transactionally after all requested terminals succeed.
Backends may fuse direct, indirect, and frame work into native transactions. The compiled view reports that fusion explicitly while replay remains attached to authored node identities.
tiers.summary: L0 says what exists, L1 composes logical passes and delays, L2 owns pure estimator math, and L3 lowers that math to scalar, Taichi, or Slang execution.

insights: A compiled plan can change physical grouping without changing authored meaning.
Backend capability claims need stage-level precision, not a single native/non-native badge.
tiers.label: Proof and source
pitfalls: Claiming ReSTIR PT is fully native because its path tracing and replay legs are native.
Letting a documentation diagram silently erase fusion or host orchestration.
prose: The scalar backend is the readable oracle. Taichi is the default interactive path, and Slang is the native portability path. Direct lighting, PT, fresh path RIS, and diffuse ReSTIR GI have accelerated native stages.
M20 remains active: ReSTIR PT correction/reduction is still host-orchestrated, and Slang PT reuse still shares the Taichi route. M21 graph composition does not close that backend-native gap.
tiers.summary: Authored topology, compiled schedules, fused dispatch groups, resource lifetimes, and graph-keyed records are separately inspectable contracts.

chapters.title: System and lowering

chapters.subtitle: Direct light points and indirect paths share an image, not a reservoir contract.

insights: Reuse means combining compatible samples in the correct domain.
A reservoir is constant-size state representing many candidates.
tiers.label: Orientation
pitfalls: Calling every retained sample a light sample hides path-space support and Jacobians.
Comparing candidate count while ignoring ray work gives misleading quality claims.
prose: NEE, RIS, and ReSTIR DI progressively enrich candidate selection while preserving one deferred visibility test. PT, path RIS, ReSTIR GI, and ReSTIR PT instead manipulate complete contribution paths and may need replay or reconnection work.
Both branches meet only when emission, direct radiance, and indirect radiance are composed at the primary hit.
tiers.summary: The direct branch chooses where light comes from now; the indirect branch chooses a multi-bounce history by which light arrived.

insights: M counts represented candidates, not update calls.
Identity-area reuse has J=1; hybrid path reconnection generally does not.
tiers.label: Working model
pitfalls: Overloading direct evaluate with path replay breaks the one-shadow-ray invariant.
Dropping failed inverse mappings from correction math can create plausible, spreading bias.
prose: The direct Reservoir selects a LightSample in emitter-area measure. Fresh proposals, temporal aggregates, and spatial aggregates stream through weighted reservoir sampling; evaluate traces the one deferred shadow ray exactly once.

The PathReservoir selects a PathContribution with compact reproduction identity, RGB contribution, scalar target, represented count, and shift lineage. Exact reuse evaluates support, inverse support, generalized balance terms, visibility, and a mapping Jacobian.
tiers.summary: Direct lighting retains propose/evaluate; indirect transport uses explicit trace/resample/shift/evaluate contracts.

insights: Unbiasedness is an expectation claim and needs statistical tests.
Forward validity alone is insufficient; exact reuse also needs inverse support.
tiers.label: Proof and source
pitfalls: Using cached radiance without naming the approximation.
Assuming J=1 after leaving the shared emitter-area identity mapping.
prose: Fresh path RIS statistically agrees with the unchanged depth-limited PT integral. Exact spatial and temporal GRIS preserve normalized proposal terms, while named biased modes remain explicit experiments.
General-material hybrid shifts replay from a common origin, reconnect at a supported vertex, and compose factored Jacobians. Stable typed failures are zero-support evidence, not missing records.
tiers.summary: Correctness lives in measures, support, target values, generalized balance weights, and disclosed work—not in a visually plausible frame.

chapters.title: Sampling domains

chapters.subtitle: Deterministic addresses and immutable stages make reuse parallel, replayable, and portable.

insights: Determinism is an architectural feature, not only a test convenience.
Freeze-then-gather replaces synchronization and atomics with ownership.
tiers.label: Orientation
pitfalls: A stateful RNG makes replay depend on unrelated control flow.
In-place spatial updates make results depend on thread or scan order.
prose: Counter-based RNG turns randomness into a lookup keyed by pixel, sample, frame, bounce, and stream. There is no mutable global sequence for unrelated work to disturb.
Temporal reuse reads the preceding committed frame. Spatial reuse first freezes the post-temporal image, then each pixel gathers neighbors and writes only itself.
tiers.summary: Every random draw has an address; every pixel owns its output; reuse reads frozen neighbors or prior frames.

insights: SoA is the common ABI across numpy, Taichi fields, Slang buffers, and eventual WGSL storage.
Expanded vertices are temporary or selected-pixel evidence, never persistent image-wide state.
tiers.label: Working model
pitfalls: Copying variable-length paths per pixel explodes memory and UI complexity.
Treating a second cook in the same frame as a second history update violates transactional semantics.
prose: FrameOutputs exposes typed zero-copy views over scalar arrays. Direct and path histories snapshot prior cameras, G-buffers, compact reservoirs, and configuration identity without storing expanded paths per pixel.

L1 delay nodes read the preceding committed value and stage a current value. Semantic edits reset history; layout and display edits do not. Multiple terminals share one transaction and one upstream cook.
tiers.summary: Compact SoA histories carry just enough state to validate, clamp, shift, and regenerate selected contributions.

insights: History rejection is a typed result worth inspecting.
One-writer/no-atomics is tested in source and behavior, not left as a comment.
tiers.label: Proof and source
pitfalls: Keeping history after an incompatible semantic edit contaminates every later frame.
Testing only final RGB can miss divergent discrete state that happens to look similar.
prose: Tests check unique deterministic neighbor offsets, camera reprojection, primitive/depth/normal/domain rejection, M-clamping, unchanged first-frame behavior, and scalar/accelerated retained-state parity.

Recorder presence cannot change traced contributions, selected candidates, radiance, random draws, or visibility work. Capture resume reconstructs exactly the history that uninterrupted rendering would have supplied.
tiers.summary: Ownership, immutability, history compatibility, and RNG independence are executable invariants.

chapters.title: State, space, and time

chapters.subtitle: A pixel is a compact proof object that can unfold into paths, decisions, failures, and views.

insights: The record is the introspection substrate.
Failure is first-class explanatory data.
tiers.label: Orientation
pitfalls: Re-tracing extra visibility rays for visualization creates an observer effect.
A screenshot-only debugger cannot explain reservoir ancestry or correction math.
prose: Clicking a pixel replays the exact completed RNG batch through the scalar oracle. The record contains the primary hit, direct candidates, path vertices, reservoir updates, temporal and spatial lineage, mapping failures, correction terms, and final composition.
The path tree, charts, 2D maps, and orbitable 3D territory are folds of that record, so changing the view does not change the sample.
tiers.summary: A screenshot is the result; a replay record explains why that result occurred.

insights: One compact selected payload can unfold into a complete selected-pixel explanation.
Cross-view identity matters more than duplicating labels in every representation.
tiers.label: Working model
pitfalls: Searching for a convenient fixture at build time makes the narrative silently drift.
Letting sandbox edits overwrite evidence confuses explanation with experiment.
prose: Pixel (11, 14) at frame 5 is replayed after capturing frame 4 history. Five fresh contributions, one accepted temporal reconnection, and six spatial attempts—including typed failures—produce a final reservoir representing M=41 candidates.
Stable entity IDs link a chart row, lineage marker, evidence table, DSL form, and 3D shifted path. Counterfactual WRS and Jacobian sliders are visually separated from the immutable recorded values.
tiers.summary: The checked-in fixture follows one glossy ReSTIR PT sample from fresh path contributions through temporal and spatial GRIS to final radiance.

insights: Discrete state, float buffers, statistical expectation, and performance are different proof obligations.
Source anchors make every architectural claim navigable to code, tests, or an approved specification.
tiers.label: Proof and source
pitfalls: One deterministic fixture cannot prove unbiasedness by itself.
Sharing implementation code with the oracle weakens differential evidence even if tests pass.
prose: Generation fails if the pinned proof shape changes: six vertices, five contributions, one temporal shift, six spatial attempts, three valid and three failed spatial mappings, two accepted spatial updates, and final M=41.
Scalar/Taichi comparisons require exact discrete agreement; native GPU floats use documented tight tolerances. Statistical tests separately validate convergence and equal-budget quality claims.
tiers.summary: The canonical fixture, generated images, graph projection, replay payload, and manifest are reproducible checked artifacts.

chapters.title: Proof and introspection

chapters.subtitle: Keep the proof disciplines; move a few contracts earlier; resist turning the lab into a production renderer.

insights: Progressive lowering kept every milestone runnable.
Visceral inspection and mathematical correctness reinforced each other.
tiers.label: Orientation
pitfalls: Optimizing a plausible but incorrect reuse mapping only spreads the error faster.
Broad production-renderer scope would bury the estimator research payload.
prose: Each epoch added one conceptual burden—interactivity, reuse, persistence, path space, materials, native execution, or graph composition—only after the prior contract became observable and testable.
The most reusable lesson is to make correctness explainable before optimizing it. ReSTIR errors are often visually plausible and spread through space and time.
tiers.summary: The project succeeded by growing through bounded vertical slices while keeping a small set of invariants green.

insights: Move infrastructure earlier only when a concrete estimator contract needs it.
A curated graph is enough; arbitrary plugins and a shader compiler remain unnecessary.
tiers.label: Working model
pitfalls: Introducing the graph before there are stable domains invites abstractions around imaginary needs.
Waiting until final native hardening to design replay ABIs leaves host orchestration debt.
prose: On a restart, define record and capture identities with the initial scalar spine, introduce strict scene data before multiplying built-ins, and model transactional delays when temporal reuse first appears.

Design the accelerated transient-vertex ABI before general-material hybrid reuse. Add curated graph composition after estimator contracts exist, but before UI and capture accumulate more configuration-specific orchestration.
tiers.summary: Keep domain separation, the independent oracle, counter RNG, immutable stages, exact defaults, and compact lineage; introduce several supporting contracts earlier.

insights: A finished later milestone does not imply every earlier hardening milestone is complete.
Documentation should encode caveats as tested claims, not prose that can silently age.
tiers.label: Proof and source
pitfalls: Rewriting history to make the architecture look cleaner hides why safeguards exist.
A single backend badge obscures precisely where portability work remains.
prose: The project should still defer meshes, textures, animation, volumes, denoising, and production frame-time targets. Analytic scenes and fixed-depth transport keep support, Jacobian, and replay evidence tractable.

Do not mark M20 complete until native ReSTIR PT correction/reduction, Slang PT staging, remaining performance gates, and final smoke artifacts satisfy its execution packet. M21 is complete but deliberately orthogonal.
tiers.summary: The roadmap records both the successful disciplines and the remaining native-backend debt; the retrospective must preserve both.
